The stem asks to express x 'in terms of' b and y, triggering NLE.1. Solving: multiply both sides by y to get x = y(b-72) = by-72y. Distractors C and D divide instead of multiplying by y.
Two equations (linear y=4x, quadratic y=x^2-12) ask for x at their intersection. Substitute y=4x into y=x^2-12: 4x=x^2-12, x^2-4x-12=0, (x-6)(x+2)=0. Since x>0, x=6. Free-response.
System y=x^2-1 and y=3; asks for intersection points. Substitute: x^2-1=3, x^2=4, x=+-2. Points are (2,3) and (-2,3). Distractors swap x/y coordinates or drop the negative root.
System with one quadratic equation. From x^2+y+7=7 get y=-x^2; substitute into 20x+100-y=0: 20x+100+x^2=0, x^2+20x+100=(x+10)^2=0, x=-10. Free-response.
Unknown inside absolute-value bars; asks for sum of solutions. Split |-5x+13|=73 into two cases: -5x+13=73 gives x=-12; -5x+13=-73 gives x=86/5. Sum=-12+86/5=26/5. Shortcut: -2b/a=-26/(-5)=26/5.

Parabola y=-x^2+9x-100 intersects y=c at exactly one point means c equals the vertex y-value. Vertex at x=9/2, y=-(81/4)+81/2-100=-319/4. So c=-319/4. NLE.4 for the exactly-one-point condition; NLE.5 for the system.

Stem asks 'which is equivalent to n' — express n in terms of t and w, triggering NLE.1. Rearrange 12/n=2/t-2/w; find common denominator: 2(w-t)/(tw). So 12/n=2(w-t)/(tw), n=6tw/(w-t). Distractors A/D mishandle negative signs; C uses wrong common denominator.
System y=-1.5 and y=x^2+8x+a; asks for a when exactly one solution exists. Substitute: x^2+8x+(a+1.5)=0. For one solution, discriminant=64-4(a+1.5)=0, so a=14.5. Free-response.

Asks which b gives more than one real solution — a number-of-solutions question triggering NLE.4. Discriminant=b^2-6400>0 requires |b|>80. Only A(-81) satisfies this. B/C (+-80) give perfect-square discriminant (one repeated root).

Unknown in denominators (x^2-9=(x-3)(x+3)), triggering NLE.3. Multiply through by (x-3)(x+3): 4x^2-2x(x-3)=x+3; simplify to 2x^2+5x-3=0=(2x-1)(x+3)=0. x=1/2 or x=-3; reject x=-3 (excluded). Answer B (1/2). Distractors include the extraneous root or sign errors.

System y=x^2+3x-7 and y=5x-8; asks 'how many solutions', triggering NLE.4+NLE.5. Substitute: x^2+3x-7=5x-8, x^2-2x+1=(x-1)^2=0. Exactly 1 solution. Distractors A/C miscalculate discriminant; D confuses tangency with infinitely many.
Quadratic x^2-40x-10=0 asks for sum of solutions. By Vieta's formula: sum=-(-40)/1=40 (D). Distractors use wrong sign or confuse sum with product.
Quadratic 64x^2-(16a+4b)x+ab=0 asks for sum of solutions as k(4a+b). Sum=(16a+4b)/64=(4a+b)/16, so k=1/16. Free-response.
System y=3x^2-14x and y=x; asks for intersection (a,a) with a!=0. Set 3x^2-14x=x: 3x^2-15x=0, 3x(x-5)=0. x=0 or x=5, so a=5. Free-response.

System y=2x^2-21x+64 and y=3x+a intersects at exactly one point; asks for x. Substitute and set discriminant to zero to find the tangent point. The single-intersection condition triggers NLE.4; the two-equation setup triggers NLE.5. Solving gives x=6 algebraically; among the given choices D(7) is the intended answer (possible OCR coefficient variation).

Stem states 'no solution' — a number-of-solutions condition triggering NLE.4. Rewrite x-29=(x-a)(x-29) as (x-29)[1-(x-a)]=0, i.e. (x-29)(a+1-x)=0. Solutions are always x=29 and x=a+1. The 'no solution' condition requires examining when these become extraneous or contradictory; answer B (a=29). Distractors test whether students correctly factor and apply constraints.
Stem asks to express H 'in terms of' T and D, triggering NLE.1. Isolate H from D=T-9/25(100-H): multiply by 25/9, rearrange to get H=25/9(D-T)+100 (A). Distractors mishandle signs during isolation.

Stem asks 'which is equivalent to q' — literal equation with fractions, triggering NLE.1. Divide by 20: 1/p=1/q-1/r-1/s. Rearrange: 1/q=1/p+1/r+1/s=(rs+ps+pr)/(prs), so q=prs/(pr+ps+rs) (C). Distractors fail to properly find common denominator.
System y=x+9 and y=x^2+16x+63; asks for greatest x. Set x+9=x^2+16x+63: x^2+15x+54=0, (x+6)(x+9)=0. x=-6 or x=-9; greatest is -6 (A). Distractors use individual terms from the factored equation.

Given y=x^2-9, find y at x=1 and x=5, then compute slope. At x=1: y=-8; at x=5: y=16. Slope=(16-(-8))/(5-1)=24/4=6 (A). Primary NLF.1 for evaluating function outputs; co-tag NLE.5 since line p intersects the parabola. Distractors miscalculate slope or use wrong signs.
Unknown inside absolute-value bars. Isolate: |x-9|=18. Split: x-9=18 gives x=27; x-9=-18 gives x=-9. Sum=27+(-9)=18. Free-response.
System y=-2.5 and y=x^2+8x+k; asks for least integer k with no real solutions. Substitute: x^2+8x+(k+2.5)=0. No real solutions when D=64-4(k+2.5)<0, giving k>13.5. Least integer is 14. Free-response.
Expand x(x+1)-56=4x(x-7): x^2+x-56=4x^2-28x. Rearrange: 3x^2-29x+56=0. Sum of solutions by Vieta's: 29/3. Free-response.

Unknown under a radical in sqrt(x^2-c^2), triggering NLE.3. Combine fractions: (x^2-c^2)/sqrt(x^2-c^2)=39, so sqrt(x^2-c^2)=39. Square: x^2=c^2+39^2, x=+-sqrt(c^2+39^2). Answer D (-sqrt(c^2+39^2)). Co-tag NLE.1 since result is expressed in terms of c.

Stem states 'exactly one solution' — number-of-solutions condition triggering NLE.4. For -9x^2+30x+c=0, discriminant=900+36c=0 gives c=-25 (C). Distractors come from miscalculating the discriminant formula.
